3.author: St. John Chrysostom
3.work: Homilies on the Gospel of St. John, Homily 24
3.text: Chrysostom hears in 'unless one is born from above' a single uncompromising verdict on the natural state of every human being, learned and unlearned, Jewish and Gentile alike. Nicodemus is a teacher in Israel, and yet he stands here on the same threshold as every catechumen. The Kingdom of God is not entered by being a son of Abraham, by being well-instructed, or by being virtuous. It is entered only by a new birth, given by God, into a life that does not begin from the flesh.

5.author: St. John Chrysostom
5.work: Homilies on the Gospel of St. John, Homily 25
5.text: Chrysostom takes 'water and the Spirit' together as the Lord's plain naming of Baptism. The water is real water, the rite is real, but what is given through it is the Holy Spirit. The Spirit comes upon the water, and the candidate emerges not as he went in. Chrysostom is direct: this is the only door into the Kingdom Christ Himself has named. To ask after another way is to ask for what God has not given.

5.author: St. Cyril of Alexandria
5.work: Commentary on the Gospel of John, Book 2
5.text: Cyril reads 'water and the Spirit' as a single sacramental gift, not a sequence of two events. The water alone is rite; the Spirit alone, without the visible form Christ instituted, is not the way the Lord has appointed for us. In Baptism the Spirit hallows the water, and the candidate is born from God by the very life of the Holy Trinity entering the soul. The Kingdom is entered here, in a font and a name, because the King willed it so.

16.author: St. Augustine of Hippo
16.work: Tractates on the Gospel of John, Tractate 12
16.text: Augustine refuses to soften the universality of 'God so loved the world.' The world that is loved is the world that nailed Him to the cross. It is the world of those who hate Him, of those who do not yet know Him, of those whom Christians have not yet imagined as objects of grace. The Father gave the Son not because the world deserved Him but because the world needed Him. Whoever believes does not perish; whoever does not believe is condemned already, not by a sentence newly imposed, but by remaining outside the only life that is given.
